text:
Alex: FYI Sales is pushing AcmeCorp — they want p95 <= 50ms at ~200 qps. Is that realistic on hosted?
Maria: Product question — do they mean p95 server-side only or end-to-end (client + network)?
Alex: Sales said 'API latency' in the contract brief, not specific. They said they’ll switch vendors if we can’t guarantee.
Sam: eng-runtime: short answer: not on shared hosted with our current microbatch & kernels unless they have great KV reuse or we give them dedicated. Quick numbers below.
Sam: ```
baseline hosted v1.8.2, 200 qps, microbatch=16
p50: 18ms
p95: 72ms
p99: 150ms
kv-cache hit: 28%
after kernel v1.9.0 opt (faster matmul):
p95 -> 58ms, p99 -> 120ms
```
Jess: eng-ml: KV cache hit-rate is the single biggest swing. If Acme's traffic has high prefix reuse (chatty retrievers, short prompts) and we hit 45%+, p95 can drop under 50ms. If they're low-reuse (long prompts, diverse queries) we won't.
Kevin: eng-sre: Other levers: route Acme to lower-latency pool (shorter max_seq), or offer a dedicated GPU pool with tuned microbatching. Also consider front-door caching + edge TTL for repeated system prompts.
Sam: microbatch sizing note: microbatch=4 gives better tail but reduces net throughput. At synthetic 200 qps:
- microbatch=16 -> p95 72ms (high throughput)
- microbatch=8 -> p95 54ms (throughput -15%)
- microbatch=4 -> p95 46ms (throughput -30%)
So it's a direct latency vs throughput tradeoff.
Maria: Product: OK we need an options doc for Sales to present: (A) Shared hosted w/ relaxed SLO (p95 70ms), (B) Dedicated pool with SLA p95 50ms (price uplift), (C) Pilot + auto-fallback routing + credits. Also call out p99 behavior and the tails risk.
Alex: Can we run a canary emulating Acme traffic shape? Jess / Sam can we spin one for a week?
Jess: Yes. I'll replay their anonymized traces (historical prompts) and vary KV hit from 20% -> 60%. Expect p95 ~48-52ms if kv-hit >=45%. If kv-hit = 20% p95 stays ~70ms.
Sam: Also flag: we observed a perf regression in a recent kernel rollout where p99 spiked due to KV cache lock contention under high concurrency and long seq lenses. Patch is in PR #3842.
Sam: ```
# repro snippet we used in canary
ab -n 10000 -c 50 -p requests.json https://api.redwood.dev/generate
# tracing snippet
span: kv_cache_lock wait: median 0.2ms, p99 12ms (regression observed)
```
Kevin: Ops recommendation: offer a 2-week Dedicated pilot with telemetry. Sales can include a one-time tuning credit; during pilot we can tune microbatch and kernel selection and confirm p95/p99.
Alex: Sales: @Maria can you draft the three options and recommended phrasing? Call out explicit tradeoffs (throughput vs tail) and that p99 can't be SLA'd on shared without dedicated capacity.
Maria: On it. I'll also include a short guidance line: "If customer needs strict p95 AND p99 SLAs, recommend Dedicated + pinned model + workload profiling window."
DeployBot: deploy: canary v1.9.1 -> eng-runtime (sam) at 2026-03-16T14:12:00Z :rocket:
Sam: I'll monitor traces and post a short CSV of p50/p95/p99 by microbatch/kernel after the canary runs. :thumbsup:
